dedupe_keys.name: arches open source geospatial platform for heritage inventory and management

description: Arches is web-based geospatial software for building inventories of immovable cultural heritage: archaeological sites, buildings and other historic structures, landscapes and heritage districts. It was developed by the Getty Conservation Institute and World Monuments Fund and is maintained by the Arches Project with a community of implementers; national and city heritage agencies and UK Historic Environment Records run their own instances. Coverage: the software is global; each deployment holds its own jurisdiction's records. It stores resources as graph-based resource models built on the CIDOC CRM ontology, with map layers, controlled vocabularies (Arches Lingo), mobile field collection and a search and reporting interface. Format and access: Python and Django application installed with pip or Docker, with JSON-LD and CSV import and export and a REST API. Licence: GNU AGPL 3.0, free of charge. Caveats: Arches is a platform, not a dataset, so the data of a given instance may be public, registration-only or internal, and deployment needs PostgreSQL with PostGIS, Elasticsearch and web hosting. Simulation uses: a source of heritage asset inventories for hazard exposure and climate adaptation studies of the built environment, where an agency exports its Arches records. Related records: the Rijksmonumenten linked open data (data-rce-rijksmonumenten-cultural-heritage-objects) and the Irish NIAH inventory (data-ireland-niah-national-inventory-architectural-heritage) are heritage inventories of the same kind.
